failure_summary.description: Several trajectories used native numbers instead of JSON-string values, and one placed schema-optional filters in the required list.
Agents chose a sibling endpoint, mismatched an operation to an endpoint, or omitted a call despite an available endpoint accepting the supplied input.
Calls missed or misbound requested scope details such as locale, geographic hierarchy, hotel filters, forecast duration, or units.

patch.reasoning: The skill already explicitly covers schema placement, string serialization, endpoint matching, and facet coverage, so repeating those rules would not address a demonstrated gap. One trajectory rejected a supplied numeric location identifier even though an available endpoint accepts a generic string location. A narrow clarification can prevent that unsupported inference without weakening documented format constraints.

edits.target: - Preserve user-provided identifiers and meaningful free text unless the schema requires a documented conversion. For categorical filters, codes, and selectors, map the request to the documented parameter meaning—not a similarly named field—and use the endpoint's canonical accepted token and casing from its enums or examples. Do not pass a descriptive word as a category value when it changes the field's meaning; preserve original wording when no conversion is documented. Interpret directional constraints according to field semantics.
edits.content: - If an endpoint accepts a generic string location or identifier and its documentation does not restrict the format, pass the supplied value verbatim even if it looks unfamiliar or is not a place name. Do not reject it based on an assumed format or substitute another value.
